title: Business Analysis Advisor - Mortgage Investor Operations
description:
Position Overview

At PNC, our people are our greatest differentiator and competitive advantage in the markets we serve. We are all united in delivering the best experience for our customers. We work together each day to foster an inclusive workplace culture where all of our employees feel respected, valued and have an opportunity to contribute to the company's success. As a Business Analysis Advisor, you will be within PNC's Retail Bank Operations organization, supporting the Retail Lending Servicing and Mortgage Investor Operations group.  This position is remote.

The scope of Retail Bank Operations is impressively broad and encompasses a wide range of critical functions. These include managing the cash needs for our branch and ATM networks, printing and mailing important bank documents, and handling both inbound and outbound collections for home lending, automobile, and card services. Additionally, Retail Bank Operations focuses on loan mitigation and investor operations, developing process improvement and automation opportunities, overseeing the daily processing of cash and check deposits, bill payments, and executes strategic quality management functions.

The Retail Lending Servicing, Mortgage Investor Operations team supports mortgage servicing investor operations across Freddie Mac, Fannie Mae, Ginnie Mae, private investor portfolios, and default cash, driving process improvement, operational effectiveness, reporting, controls, and business analysis initiatives. Successful candidates will bring experience in mortgage servicing, investor reporting, loan administration, business analysis, finance, accounting, or reconciliations, along with the ability to analyze complex data, identify trends, and deliver reporting that supports strategic decision-making. Knowledge of the mortgage servicing lifecycle, including payment processing, escrow, loss mitigation, servicing transfers, MSP, default servicing, and investor reporting, is strongly preferred. This role requires collaboration across business, technology, risk, compliance, and operations partners to deliver solutions and drive continuous improvement.  In addition to the job description below, the ideal candidate will also have:  

Freddie Mac Servicing and Default Cash Postings:

Ideal candidates will have experience supporting Freddie Mac mortgage servicing operations, including investor reporting, investor accounting, loan administration, servicing transfers, remittance processes, reconciliation activities, and the interpretation and application of Freddie Mac servicing requirements. Candidates should also have experience processing and reconciling investor funds, mortgage insurance claim proceeds, liquidation proceeds, recoveries, refunds, and other default-related cash activity. Experience researching and resolving discrepancies, identifying process improvement opportunities, conducting root cause analysis, and partnering with cross-functional operational teams to strengthen controls, improve efficiency, and enhance servicing performance is highly valued.

Fannie Mae/Ginne Mae Servicing :

Ideal candidates will possess knowledge of Fannie Mae & Ginnie Mae servicing practices and investor guidelines, including reporting, reconciliation, compliance monitoring, servicing oversight, and operational support activities. Candidates should also have experience driving process improvement initiatives, identifying operational efficiencies, enhancing controls, and implementing sustainable solutions.   Successful candidates will be comfortable analyzing complex servicing requirements, translating business needs into actionable solutions, and partnering across multiple stakeholder groups. 

Private Investor & Portfolio Servicing:

Ideal candidates will have experience supporting private investor and portfolio servicing operations, including investor reporting, investor accounting, loan administration, servicing transfers, remittance processes, reconciliation activities, and the interpretation and application of investor-specific servicing requirements. Candidates should also have experience reviewing, interpreting, and operationalizing private investor servicing agreements and related contractual requirements, ensuring servicing activities, reporting obligations, remittance practices, and control processes align with investor expectations and contractual commitments. Experience supporting investor-related financial and operational processes, researching and resolving discrepancies, identifying process improvement opportunities, conducting root cause analysis, strengthening operational controls, and partnering with cross-functional teams to improve efficiency, consistency, compliance, and servicing performance is highly valued.

This position may be eligible for remote work in select geographic locations, subject to approval by PNC. If approved, work must be conducted from a quiet, secure, and confidential home-based workspace. Occasional in-office participation may be required based on business needs.

PNC will not provide sponsorship for employment visas or participate in STEM OPT for this position.

Directs the research, discovery, collection and interpretation of business requirements. Participates in the development and review of complex processes and procedures, workflow analytics and reporting. May provide senior level consultation and communicates with clients and technology teams on business designs, problem solving and business analysis to support project goals and objectives.
Consults and recommends the frameworks, methodologies and processes involved in business requirements traceability for business analysis teams. Independently mentors, leads, and coaches other associates to affect knowledge transfer. Oversees the development and maintenance of all applicable policy and procedure documentation.
Translates business needs, processes and/or procedures by partnering with applicable experts and business stakeholders

title: Commissioning Specialist
description:
Job Description Summary

Reporting to the Commissioning Manager, the Commissioning Specialist is responsible for performing the tests under GE GSI scope of work determined by the Commissioning Manager / Coordinator for the specific project according with safety, quality, and technical requirements. Working with the Commissioning Lead and Commissioning Coordinator, the Commissioning Specialist will be executing the commissioning plan with the on-site supervision of the Commissioning Lead or equivalent, performing the tests, ensuring the products and equipment reach an acceptable result as per the documentation, troubleshooting when necessary, and submitting the test reports as soon as they are finished to the team for review. It's also a responsibility of the Commissioning Specialist to provide feedback about the tests and processes to improve them and/or to correct potential gaps.

Job Description

About Us:

Come bring your energy to change the world Grid Solutions, part of the GE Vernova portfolio of energy businesses, serves customers globally with over 12,000 employees. Grid Solutions provides equipment, systems, and services to bring power reliably and efficiently from the point of generation to end power consumers. We electrify the world with advanced grid technologies and accelerate the energy transition.

GE Vernova, a dynamic accelerator comprised of our Power, Renewable Energy, Digital and Energy Financial Services businesses, is focused on leading a new era of energy - electrifying the world while simultaneously working to decarbonize it. If you are ready to make a difference and usher in a new era of energy, come join us.

Why we come to work:

At GE Vernova, we are always up for the challenge - and we're always driven to find the best solution. Our projects are unique and interesting, and you'll need to bring a solution-focused, positive approach to each one to do your best. Surrounded by committed, loyal colleagues, if you can dare to bring your ingenuity and desire to make an impact, you'll be exposed to game-changing, diverse projects that truly allow you to play your part in the green energy transition

Essential Responsibilities:

Preparation and planning phase:
Support the project execution team on commissioning matters.
Technical governance and customer relations on commissioning matters.
Plan and support pre-commissioning effort (instrumentation, documentation, etc.).

Execution phase:

Ensure work is performed safely according with GE standards and local requirements.
Contribute to overall quality and excellence in execution of commissioning.
Perform instrument functionality verification at site.
Responsible for the start-up of the various auxiliaries' system.
Conduct electrical commissioning tests on instrumentation.
Conduct commissioning tests (electrical and mechanical) of auxiliaries' systems of Substation plants and synchronous condenser facilities.
Perform the electrical test support for the start-up of Substation plants and synchronous condenser facilities.
Perform LOTO and safety preparations as required for the commissioning tests.
Provide support to the site teams regarding the technical issues or challenges.
Keep good records about site activities, work performed, issues faced and how they were dealt with (non-conformity) to provide feedback to business and support it with information in case of claims.
Collaborate in resolving complex problems.

Mandatory Qualifications / Requirements:

Strong EHS culture.
Be available for work on project sites in Canada and US.
Good understanding of electro-mechanical systems.
Ability to multitask and shift between many different projects and initiatives with tight deadlines.
Excellent interpersonal skills, teamwork skills and autonomy.
Ability to build strong customer relationships.
Demonstrated ability to work effectively with minimum supervision.
Strong customer service orientation.
Ability to navigate cross-functions and create a good rapport with other teams (Project Management, Engineering, Finance, Fleet Support, EHS, HR, etc.).
Ability to comply with mandatory requests on time, such as: trainings, timesheets, expense reports, daily reports, etc.
Understand and implement, when required, cost and schedule control for commissioning scope.
Must be proficient in French and English.

Technical:

Technical skills in programming and testing of PLC's and Controls
Testing of power distribution and delivery equipment of Low/medium Voltage Switchgear, disconnect switch, circuit breaker, capacitor bank, reactor, and Transformers.
Testing of power distribution and delivery equipment of High Voltage Switchgear, Switchgear, disconnect switch, circuit breaker, capacitor bank, reactor, and Transformers.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office (Outlook, Word, Excel, etc.) and have good computer skills.

Desired Characteristics:

Proficiency in any data acquisition software considered an asset.

Electrical or mechanical installation experience considered an asset.

title: ASIC Technical Project Manager
description:
Hudson River Trading (HRT) is seeking an ASIC Technical Project Manager to join our Hardware team. In this role, you will drive the planning and execution of complex ASIC projects, partnering with engineering teams and external vendors to deliver high performance silicon on schedule.

You will coordinate with our Software, Architecture, Design Verification (DV), Physical Design, System Design, and Data Center teams. The ideal candidate combines technical fluency in the ASIC development lifecycle with strong judgment, organization, and follow-through to identify risks early, resolve cross-functional blockers, and keep programs moving.

Responsibilities

Own integrated project plans across multiple overlapping ASIC projects, working with technical leads to define scope, milestones, dependencies, ownership, and delivery goals

Coordinate handoffs and sign-off gates across architecture, RTL, DV, physical design, implementation, manufacturing, and post-silicon activities

Track critical paths and execution cadence; surface schedule issues early and drive recovery plans with engineering leads

Assess technical, execution, partner, and quality-of-results (QoR) risks, and drive mitigation plans to closure

Run program reviews and working sessions that produce alignment and timely decisions among teams with competing priorities

Keep engineering leadership and senior management current on progress, risks, tradeoffs, and the decisions required of them

Own relationships with IP providers, implementation partners, and EDA vendors — setting deliverables, timelines, and escalation paths — and support multi-party contract negotiation and review alongside internal legal and business development

Evolve our project-management processes, reporting, and operating rhythms as the program grows

Qualifications

Experience in technical project management or engineering program management in a semiconductor, ASIC, or closely related hardware environment, backed by an electrical engineering background or hands-on involvement with ASIC projects

Working knowledge of the ASIC development lifecycle and enough technical depth to be credible with engineers across the design stack — you can follow handoffs, pressure-test estimates, and recognize where a program is likely to get stuck

A track record of delivering complex programs that span internal teams and external partners in fast-moving, ambiguous environments, including direct work with vendors on commercial terms

Strong facilitation and follow-through — you build alignment without formal authority and close loops without being chased

Proficiency with project-management and tracking tools such as Microsoft Project or Jira

Familiarity with RTL-to-GDSII execution tasks, including synthesis, DFT insertion, implementation, timing closure, ECOs, and sign-off checks preferred

The estimated base salary range for this position is $150,000 to $250,000 USD per year (or local equivalent). The base pay offered may vary depending on multiple individualized factors, including location, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. This role will also be eligible for discretionary performance-based bonuses and a competitive benefits package.

 

Culture

Hudson River Trading (HRT) brings a scientific approach to trading financial products. We have built one of the world's most sophisticated computing environments for research and development. Our researchers are at the forefront of innovation in the world of algorithmic trading. 

At HRT we welcome a variety of expertise: mathematics and computer science, physics and engineering, media and tech. We’re a community of self-starters who are motivated by the excitement of being at the cutting edge of automation in every part of our organization—from trading, to business operations, to recruiting and beyond. We value openness and transparency, and celebrate great ideas from HRT veterans and new hires alike. At HRT we’re friends and colleagues – whether we are sharing a meal, playing the latest board game, or writing elegant code. We embrace a culture of togetherness that extends far beyond the walls of our office.

Feel like you belong at HRT? Our goal is to find the best people and bring them together to do great work in a place where everyone is valued. HRT is proud of our diverse staff; we have offices all over the globe and benefit from our varied and unique perspectives. HRT is an equal opportunity employer; so whoever you are we’d love to get to know you.

description:
Job Description Summary
The energy transition is one of the defining challenges of our time - and at GE Vernova, the people behind it need to grow as fast as the work itself does. As a Learning Coordinator, you'll be the operational engine behind GE Vernova's learning programs, making sure every event, every experience, and every touchpoint is planned, delivered, and continuously improved. This is a role where your organizational precision and care for people directly shape how thousands of employees across the organization learn, develop, and succeed.

Job Description

What You'll Do
Plan and deliver learning events end to end - from calendar management and venue coordination to faculty logistics, purchase orders, and vendor relationships, for both virtual and in-person programs across multiple countries.
Own the participant experience at every stage, managing pre-event logistics, run-of-show coordination, and contingency planning to ensure smooth, high-quality delivery.
Track and report learning metrics, identify trends in program performance, and surface insights that help leaders make better decisions about development investments.
Administer learning programs within the Learning Management System (LMS) and other operational tools, maintaining accurate records and streamlined processes.
Market and communicate learning opportunities across multiple channels, helping employees at all levels understand what's available and why it matters.
Partner with Learning Leaders and Operations teams on key projects and initiatives, contributing your coordination expertise to broader talent and development priorities.
  Adhering to standard work and provide insights  for improving participant experience and simplifying standard work processes. 

Who You Are

You're someone who finds real satisfaction in making complex programs run smoothly - and in knowing that what you do behind the scenes has a direct impact on other people's growth. You're organized, adaptable, and genuinely curious about how learning works.

Required
Bachelor's Degree (preferably in OD, ID, L&D, Education, HR)
Solid experience in a learning coordination, HR, organizational development (OD), or learning and development (L&D) role - you've managed logistics for professional programs and know how to keep multiple workstreams on track
Strong written and verbal communication skills in English, with the ability to document processes, draft communications, and present information clearly
 Solid project management and organization skills. Ability to handle multiple tasks under pressure and prioritize in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment.

title: Business Analysis Advisor - Mortgage Investor Operations
description:
Position Overview

At PNC, our people are our greatest differentiator and competitive advantage in the markets we serve. We are all united in delivering the best experience for our customers. We work together each day to foster an inclusive workplace culture where all of our employees feel respected, valued and have an opportunity to contribute to the company's success. As a Business Analysis Advisor, you will be within PNC's Retail Bank Operations organization, supporting the Retail Lending Servicing and Mortgage Investor Operations group.  This position is remote.

The scope of Retail Bank Operations is impressively broad and encompasses a wide range of critical functions. These include managing the cash needs for our branch and ATM networks, printing and mailing important bank documents, and handling both inbound and outbound collections for home lending, automobile, and card services. Additionally, Retail Bank Operations focuses on loan mitigation and investor operations, developing process improvement and automation opportunities, overseeing the daily processing of cash and check deposits, bill payments, and executes strategic quality management functions.

The Retail Lending Servicing, Mortgage Investor Operations team supports mortgage servicing investor operations across Freddie Mac, Fannie Mae, Ginnie Mae, private investor portfolios, and default cash, driving process improvement, operational effectiveness, reporting, controls, and business analysis initiatives. Successful candidates will bring experience in mortgage servicing, investor reporting, loan administration, business analysis, finance, accounting, or reconciliations, along with the ability to analyze complex data, identify trends, and deliver reporting that supports strategic decision-making. Knowledge of the mortgage servicing lifecycle, including payment processing, escrow, loss mitigation, servicing transfers, MSP, default servicing, and investor reporting, is strongly preferred. This role requires collaboration across business, technology, risk, compliance, and operations partners to deliver solutions and drive continuous improvement.  In addition to the job description below, the ideal candidate will also have:  

Freddie Mac Servicing and Default Cash Postings:

Ideal candidates will have experience supporting Freddie Mac mortgage servicing operations, including investor reporting, investor accounting, loan administration, servicing transfers, remittance processes, reconciliation activities, and the interpretation and application of Freddie Mac servicing requirements. Candidates should also have experience processing and reconciling investor funds, mortgage insurance claim proceeds, liquidation proceeds, recoveries, refunds, and other default-related cash activity. Experience researching and resolving discrepancies, identifying process improvement opportunities, conducting root cause analysis, and partnering with cross-functional operational teams to strengthen controls, improve efficiency, and enhance servicing performance is highly valued.

Fannie Mae/Ginne Mae Servicing :

Ideal candidates will possess knowledge of Fannie Mae & Ginnie Mae servicing practices and investor guidelines, including reporting, reconciliation, compliance monitoring, servicing oversight, and operational support activities. Candidates should also have experience driving process improvement initiatives, identifying operational efficiencies, enhancing controls, and implementing sustainable solutions. title: Commissioning Specialist
description:
Job Description Summary

Reporting to the Commissioning Manager, the Commissioning Specialist is responsible for performing the tests under GE GSI scope of work determined by the Commissioning Manager / Coordinator for the specific project according with safety, quality, and technical requirements. Working with the Commissioning Lead and Commissioning Coordinator, the Commissioning Specialist will be executing the commissioning plan with the on-site supervision of the Commissioning Lead or equivalent, performing the tests, ensuring the products and equipment reach an acceptable result as per the documentation, troubleshooting when necessary, and submitting the test reports as soon as they are finished to the team for review. It's also a responsibility of the Commissioning Specialist to provide feedback about the tests and processes to improve them and/or to correct potential gaps.

Job Description

About Us:

Come bring your energy to change the world Grid Solutions, part of the GE Vernova portfolio of energy businesses, serves customers globally with over 12,000 employees. Grid Solutions provides equipment, systems, and services to bring power reliably and efficiently from the point of generation to end power consumers. We electrify the world with advanced grid technologies and accelerate the energy transition.

GE Vernova, a dynamic accelerator comprised of our Power, Renewable Energy, Digital and Energy Financial Services businesses, is focused on leading a new era of energy - electrifying the world while simultaneously working to decarbonize it. If you are ready to make a difference and usher in a new era of energy, come join us.

Why we come to work:

At GE Vernova, we are always up for the challenge - and we're always driven to find the best solution. Our projects are unique and interesting, and you'll need to bring a solution-focused, positive approach to each one to do your best. Surrounded by committed, loyal colleagues, if you can dare to bring your ingenuity and desire to make an impact, you'll be exposed to game-changing, diverse projects that truly allow you to play your part in the green energy transition

Essential Responsibilities:

Preparation and planning phase:
Support the project execution team on commissioning matters.
Technical governance and customer relations on commissioning matters.
Plan and support pre-commissioning effort (instrumentation, documentation, etc.).

Execution phase:

Ensure work is performed safely according with GE standards and local requirements.
Contribute to overall quality and excellence in execution of commissioning.
Perform instrument functionality verification at site.
Responsible for the start-up of the various auxiliaries' system.
Conduct electrical commissioning tests on instrumentation.
Conduct commissioning tests (electrical and mechanical) of auxiliaries' systems of Substation plants and synchronous condenser facilities.
Perform the electrical test support for the start-up of Substation plants and synchronous condenser facilities.
Perform LOTO and safety preparations as required for the commissioning tests.
Provide support to the site teams regarding the technical issues or challenges.
Keep good records about site activities, work performed, issues faced and how they were dealt with (non-conformity) to provide feedback to business and support it with information in case of claims.
Collaborate in resolving complex problems.

Mandatory Qualifications / Requirements:

Strong EHS culture.
Be available for work on project sites in Canada and US.
Good understanding of electro-mechanical systems.
Ability to multitask and shift between many different projects and initiatives with tight deadlines.
Excellent interpersonal skills, teamwork skills and autonomy.
Ability to build strong customer relationships.
Demonstrated ability to work effectively with minimum supervision.
Strong customer service orientation.
Ability to navigate cross-functions and create a good rapport with other teams (Project Management, Engineering, Finance, Fleet Support, EHS, HR, etc.).
Ability to comply with mandatory requests on time, such as: trainings, timesheets, expense reports, daily reports, etc.
Understand and implement, when required, cost and schedule control for commissioning scope.
Must be proficient in French and English.

Technical:

Technical skills in programming and testing of PLC's and Controls
Testing of power distribution and delivery equipment of Low/medium Voltage Switchgear, disconnect switch, circuit breaker, capacitor bank, reactor, and Transformers.
Testing of power distribution and delivery equipment of High Voltage Switchgear, Switchgear, disconnect switch, circuit breaker, capacitor bank, reactor, and Transformers.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office (Outlook, Word, Excel, etc.) and have good computer skills.

Desired Characteristics:

Proficiency in any data acquisition software considered an asset.

Electrical or mechanical installation experience considered an asset.

The salary range for this position is 78,800.00 - 105,000.00 - 131,200.00 USD Annual . The specific salary offered to a candidate may be influenced by a variety of factors including the candidate's experience, their education, and the work location. In addition, this position is eligible for a performance bonus.

title: Business Analysis Advisor - Mortgage Investor Operations
description:
Position Overview

At PNC, our people are our greatest differentiator and competitive advantage in the markets we serve. We are all united in delivering the best experience for our customers. We work together each day to foster an inclusive workplace culture where all of our employees feel respected, valued and have an opportunity to contribute to the company's success. As a Business Analysis Advisor, you will be within PNC's Retail Bank Operations organization, supporting the Retail Lending Servicing and Mortgage Investor Operations group.  This position is remote.

The scope of Retail Bank Operations is impressively broad and encompasses a wide range of critical functions. These include managing the cash needs for our branch and ATM networks, printing and mailing important bank documents, and handling both inbound and outbound collections for home lending, automobile, and card services. Additionally, Retail Bank Operations focuses on loan mitigation and investor operations, developing process improvement and automation opportunities, overseeing the daily processing of cash and check deposits, bill payments, and executes strategic quality management functions.

The Retail Lending Servicing, Mortgage Investor Operations team supports mortgage servicing investor operations across Freddie Mac, Fannie Mae, Ginnie Mae, private investor portfolios, and default cash, driving process improvement, operational effectiveness, reporting, controls, and business analysis initiatives. Successful candidates will bring experience in mortgage servicing, investor reporting, loan administration, business analysis, finance, accounting, or reconciliations, along with the ability to analyze complex data, identify trends, and deliver reporting that supports strategic decision-making. Knowledge of the mortgage servicing lifecycle, including payment processing, escrow, loss mitigation, servicing transfers, MSP, default servicing, and investor reporting, is strongly preferred. This role requires collaboration across business, technology, risk, compliance, and operations partners to deliver solutions and drive continuous improvement.  In addition to the job description below, the ideal candidate will also have:  

Freddie Mac Servicing and Default Cash Postings:

Ideal candidates will have experience supporting Freddie Mac mortgage servicing operations, including investor reporting, investor accounting, loan administration, servicing transfers, remittance processes, reconciliation activities, and the interpretation and application of Freddie Mac servicing requirements. Candidates should also have experience processing and reconciling investor funds, mortgage insurance claim proceeds, liquidation proceeds, recoveries, refunds, and other default-related cash activity. Experience researching and resolving discrepancies, identifying process improvement opportunities, conducting root cause analysis, and partnering with cross-functional operational teams to strengthen controls, improve efficiency, and enhance servicing performance is highly valued.

Fannie Mae/Ginne Mae Servicing :

Ideal candidates will possess knowledge of Fannie Mae & Ginnie Mae servicing practices and investor guidelines, including reporting, reconciliation, compliance monitoring, servicing oversight, and operational support activities. Candidates should also have experience driving process improvement initiatives, identifying operational efficiencies, enhancing controls, and implementing sustainable solutions.   Successful candidates will be comfortable analyzing complex servicing requirements, translating business needs into actionable solutions, and partnering across multiple stakeholder groups. 

Private Investor & Portfolio Servicing:

Ideal candidates will have experience supporting private investor and portfolio servicing operations, including investor reporting, investor accounting, loan administration, servicing transfers, remittance processes, reconciliation activities, and the interpretation and application of investor-specific servicing requirements. Candidates should also have experience reviewing, interpreting, and operationalizing private investor servicing agreements and related contractual requirements, ensuring servicing activities, reporting obligations, remittance practices, and control processes align with investor expectations and contractual commitments. Experience supporting investor-related financial and operational processes, researching and resolving discrepancies, identifying process improvement opportunities, conducting root cause analysis, strengthening operational controls, and partnering with cross-functional teams to improve efficiency, consistency, compliance, and servicing performance is highly valued.

This position may be eligible for remote work in select geographic locations, subject to approval by PNC. If approved, work must be conducted from a quiet, secure, and confidential home-based workspace. Occasional in-office participation may be required based on business needs.

PNC will not provide sponsorship for employment visas or participate in STEM OPT for this position.

Job Description
Directs the research, discovery, collection and interpretation of business requirements. Participates in the development and review of complex processes and procedures, workflow analytics and reporting. May provide senior level consultation and communicates with clients and technology teams on business designs, problem solving and business analysis to support project goals and objectives.
Consults and recommends the frameworks, methodologies and processes involved in business requirements traceability for business analysis teams. Independently mentors, leads, and coaches other associates to affect knowledge transfer. Oversees the development and maintenance of all applicable policy and procedure documentation.
Translates business needs, processes and/or procedures by partnering with applicable experts and business stakeholders

Technical governance and customer relations on commissioning matters.

title: Knowledge Management Specialist
description:
Who We Are

KeepTruckin builds technology using the latest advancements in AI and computer vision to improve the safety and efficiency of businesses with vehicles. Over one million drivers and 100,000 companies across every industry trust KeepTruckin’s integrated platform to power their operations, prevent accidents and reduce costs.  

At KeepTruckin, we see our hard work rewarded in tangible ways every day, and we believe that intelligence is most powerful when paired with humility. We’re motivated by the opportunity to save lives on the road while impacting and improving every facet of multiple trillion-dollar industries that keep our physical economy moving. KeepTruckin is proud to be a Forbes Cloud 100 company, Forbes Best Startup Employer 2020, and an Inc Magazine Best Place to Work.

About the Role:

Join the team focused on strategically using content to optimize performance of Sales and Customer Success employees at KeepTruckin. The KeepTruckin Sales Enablement Knowledge Management (KM) team is seeking a KM Specialist to help us scale and optimize KT sellers’ and success specialists’ collective repository of needle-moving knowledge. In this role, you will have the opportunity to help shape and deliver knowledge management strategies and to continuously improve knowledge management platforms. Your responsibilities will include partnering with enablement, sales, and customer success staff to define, capture, and manage knowledge in support of proven sales & customer success tactics. You will help to accelerate the sales process within the world’s leading ELD and fleet management platform provider. The KM Specialist inspires a continuous improvement mindset within Sales Enablement, partners with subject matter experts and other stakeholders within the company, and implements changes in a timely manner to advance the curation and usage of knowledge. The ideal candidate will possess a background that enables them to structure and develop internal content that directly supports KeepTruckin’s Sales and Customer Success employees.

What You'll Do:

Partner with stakeholders and subject matter experts to systematically collect voice of customer information, validate content relevance, and Identify problems/solutions to be captured in assigned knowledge domain(s)

Intake and triage requests for knowledge content

Identify and capture new information on an ongoing basis

Build collaborative knowledge sharing environments, motivating individual contribution of insights and best practices

Perform page and platform audits to assure/maintain a high standard of KMS quality 

Manage special projects focused on continuously improving the knowledge management system, including new content creation, governance, communications, voice of customer, and more.

Facilitate discussions with and feedback from the KM Coach community, a group of front line subject matter experts who direct feedback from the field to the KM team and act as super users of the Knowledge Management System (KMS).

What We're Looking For:

3+ years of professional experience in sales, customer success, knowledge management, content creation, or content strategy.

3+ years of working with communications channels (e.g. Confluence, Slack, etc.) and familiarity and expertise with content creation tools, including blogs, email templates, and videos

Bachelor’s degree in business, communications, marketing, or a related field, or equivalent hands-on experience

Clear track record of managing projects while demonstrating excellent business judgement

Strong written and verbal communicator who can drive consensus and articulate recommendations

Strong organizational, planning, and communication skills, problem solving skills, and team-orientated philosophy; great attention to detail and pride in execution of initiatives

Creating a diverse and inclusive workplace is one of KeepTruckin's core values. We are an equal opportunity employer and welcome people of different backgrounds, experiences, abilities and perspectives.

title: Process Management Associate, Provider Operations
description:
Hi, we're Oscar. We're hiring a Process Management Associate to join our Network Operations Team.
 
Oscar is the first health insurance company built around a full stack technology platform and a relentless focus on serving our members. We started Oscar in 2012 to create the kind of health insurance company we would want for ourselves-one that behaves like a doctor in the family.
 
About the role:
 
We are seeking a detail-oriented and analytical Process Management Associate to join our Network Operations Team. The primary responsibility of this role is to create, analyze and evaluate existing business processes, identify areas for improvement, and develop and implement effective process improvement strategies. The Process Management Analyst will work closely with cross-functional teams to ensure process optimization, efficiency, and effectiveness.
 
You will report into the Director, Process Improvement.
 
Work Location: This is a remote position, open to candidates who reside in: Atlanta, Georgia. You will be fully remote; however, our approach to work may adapt over time. Future models could potentially involve a hybrid presence at the hub office associated with your metro area. #LI-Remote
 
Pay Transparency: The base pay for this role is: $87,188 - $114,434 per year. You are also eligible for employee benefits, participation in Oscar's unlimited vacation program and annual performance bonuses.
 
Responsibilities:
  Conduct comprehensive analysis of existing business processes, including process mapping, data collection, and identifying areas for improvement.
 Collaborate with stakeholders to gather requirements and determine process improvement objectives.
 Develop and implement process improvement strategies, including the creation of process documentation, standard operating procedures, and workflow diagrams.
 Utilize process management methodologies, such as Lean Six Sigma, to identify bottlenecks, inefficiencies, and areas of waste within existing processes.
 Facilitate process improvement workshops and meetings, providing guidance and support to cross-functional teams.
 Lead or participate in process improvement projects, ensuring successful implementation and achievement of desired outcomes.
 Monitor and track process performance using appropriate metrics and tools, identifying trends and areas requiring further attention.
 Prepare and present reports and recommendations to management, summarizing findings, progress, and outcomes of process improvement initiatives.
 Collaborate with Technology, Product, and Engineering teams to identify and implement process automation opportunities.
 Stay updated on industry best practices and emerging trends in process management, continually seeking opportunities to enhance processes and drive efficiencies.
  Compliance with all applicable laws and regulations 
  Other duties as assigned 
  
Requirements:
  A bachelor's degree or 3+ years commensurate experience
 3+ years of work experience in process management, process improvement or similar.
 2+ years of experience using process management methodologies, such as Lean Six Sigma, BPMN, or similar frameworks.
 2+ years of experience with end to end process management and mapping
  
Bonus points:
  2+ years of experience using data software such as Excel, SQL, Python or other data analytics tools
 Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Business Administration, or other related field
 Lean Six Sigma Green Belt certification or higher

title: Private Wealth Management Registered Client Service Associate
description:
POSITION SUMMARY:

Registered Client Service Associates provide exceptional service to our clients and support Financial Advisor(s) (FAs)/ Private Wealth Advisor(s) (PWAs)/ teams on a daily basis. Through regular interactions with clients, individuals in this role build trusted relationships. Leading with a client first mindset, a successful candidate for this role will have strong interpersonal skills and will be able to assist clients with their everyday needs. 

DUTIES and RESPONSIBILITIES:

CLIENT SUPPORT

Provide service coverage for a FA/PWA/team including:  
Supporting the FA/PWA/team in cultivating and enhancing new and existing client relationships
Executing money movement transactions at the request of the client and/or FA/PWA/team
Answering general non-investment related questions concerning client accounts, including relaying stock positions, and providing account balances (e.g., funds due and margin debit)
Enter profile information or pre-fill account documentation on client accounts and/or documents in aa clerical capacity at the direction of the client and/or FA/PWA/team
Educating or enrolling clients in digital tools (e.g. MSOnline, eSign, eAuthorization)
Onboard and maintain client accounts, including collecting client information and required documentation in a clerical capacity at the direction of the client and/or FA/PWA/team
Provide existing clients with details around their account information (e.g., investment objectives, risk tolerance) 
Accept or enter unsolicited orders and/or enter solicited orders in a clerical capacity at the direction of the FA/PWA/team
Supporting the FAs / PWAs / teams' marketing strategy (e.g., website maintenance) 
Assist FAs / PWAs/ teams in delivering against their business plan and client service model
Remaining current on all policies, procedures, and new platforms
Participating in firm initiatives (e.g., training or education programs), special projects and/or other duties directed by local management

ADMINISTRATIVE SUPPORT
Answering inbound phone calls or making outbound calls with updates on service requests (e.g., scheduling follow-up calls with FAs / PWAs / teams as needed) 
Managing the calendar including coordinating meetings or events with logistics such as material prep (e.g., maintaining agendas, sending calendar invites with Zoom credentials) 
Maintaining travel itineraries, preparing expense reports and managing the reimbursement process
Assisting with general in-office support functions such as copying, filing and scanning documentation 
 Preparing and submitting expense reports for processing at the direction of the FA/PWA

EDUCATION, EXPERIENCE, KNOWLEDGE, and SKILLS:

Education and/or Experience 
High School Diploma/Equivalency
College degree preferred
Active Series 7 (GS), and Series 66 (AG/RA) or Series 63 (AG) and Series 65 (RA)
Two or more years of industry experience preferred

Knowledge/Skills
Knowledge of financial services products, including but not limited to equities, bonds, options, mutual funds, annuities, insurance, and managed accounts
Detail orientated with superior organizational skills and ability to prioritize 
Advanced Microsoft Office skills (Word, Excel, Outlook and PowerPoint)
Exceptional writing, interpersonal and client service skills
Strong time management skills
Team player with the ability to collaborate with others
Ability to work in a fast-paced, evolving environment
Adaptable and ability to multitask
 Goal oriented, self-motivated and results driven

Reports To:

Business Service Officer

WHAT YOU CAN EXPECT FROM MORGAN STANLEY: 

At Morgan Stanley, we raise, manage and allocate capital for our clients - helping them reach their goals. We do it in a way that's differentiated - and we've done that for 90 years.  Our values - putting clients first, doing the right thing, leading with exceptional ideas, committing to diversity and inclusion, and giving back - aren't just beliefs, they guide the decisions we make every day to do what's best for our clients, communities and more than 80,000 employees in 1,200 offices across 42 countries. At Morgan Stanley, you'll find an opportunity to work alongside the best and the brightest, in an environment where you are supported and empowered. Our teams are relentless collaborators and creative thinkers, fueled by their diverse backgrounds and experiences. We are proud to support our employees and their families at every point along their work-life journey, offering some of the most attractive and comprehensive employee benefits and perks in the industry. There's also ample opportunity to move about the business for those who show passion and grit in their work.

title: Risk Management - Climate, Nature & Social (CN&S) Risk Associate
description:
JPMorganChase (JPMC) is committed to understanding how climate change and nature and social-related factors may drive or influence the risks we identify and manage. This includes evaluating how our business and the activities of our clients and customers could be impacted through the transition to a low-carbon economy and physical risks driven by climate change. The Climate, Nature and Social (CN&S) Risk team's firmwide mandate is to set risk management framework and strategies, design risk scenarios, and build a unified approach for firmwide implementation to address the dynamic climate, nature and social risk landscape. The team collaborates with stakeholders across the firm to integrate climate, nature, and social considerations into risk management frameworks, including those of credit risk and market risk.

As an Associate on the CN&S Risk team, you will play an important role in shaping the firm's approach to managing these risks. The ideal candidate is a self-starter with experience in financial risk analysis, cross-functional collaboration, and the ability to synthesize technical content into effective written materials for both internal and external audiences. This is an exciting opportunity to contribute to a rapidly evolving field within the financial services industry, with high focus and visibility within J.P. Morgan.

Job Responsibilities 

Conduct deep-dive research, literature reviews, and analysis on climate, nature and social risk topics affecting the firm's portfolio, producing insightful summaries and intelligence reports for senior management and various internal working groups.
Apply financial risk management expertise (e.g., credit risk frameworks and methodologies) to deliver cross-line of business projects that assess and manage the transmission of climate, nature, and social risks across the firm's risk types and portfolios.
Develop high-quality presentations, written materials, and internal reports for both internal stakeholders and external disclosures, focusing on effective communication of technical and quantitative information around climate, nature and social risk topics.
Track regulatory deliverables and inputs required from the team, perform regulatory horizon scanning, and share regulatory alerts and summaries with the wider team.
Identify and pilot appropriate analytics and AI/GenAI use cases to enhance CN&S risk insights and communications, partnering with stakeholders to ensure appropriate governance, controls, and documentation.
Stay informed of the latest industry trends and advancements in climate, nature, and social risk management within the financial services industry.

Required Qualifications, Capabilities, and Skills

Bachelor's degree in economics, finance, public policy, or related field. 
Experience in credit/counterparty and/or market risk management is required
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to synthesize technical information and extract key messages clearly and accurately.
Strong written and verbal communication skills, with experience synthesizing technical information and extracting key messages clearly, accurately, and succinctly for senior audiences.
Ability to prioritize and execute tasks independently and as part of a team, with attention to detail and accuracy.
Proficiency in Microsoft Excel, PowerPoint, and Word.

Preferred Qualifications, Capabilities, and Skills

Minimum 2 plus years of experience in the financial services industry, with strong preference given to candidates with a master's degree and/or background in credit risk or financial risk management. 
Knowledge of climate and environmental risk is highly preferred
Familiarity with derivative products and enterprise risk management processes is a plus.
Experience in a climate-related role (i.e. climate consulting or research) working with financial institutions is a plus.
Familiarity with interpreting technical data and analytics is an advantage.

description:
Join the Corporate Development team at Chase, which is broadly responsible for strategic partnerships, investments, and acquisitions across Chase's consumer lines of business - Consumer Bank, Business Bank, Wealth Management, Card Services, Connected Commerce, Home Lending, and Auto Lending. These initiatives are critical to Chase's ability to execute on its core strategies and meet the needs of our customers in a rapidly changing financial services ecosystem. You will have the opportunity to develop and lead these strategic initiatives that require careful consideration as well as a relentless focus on execution.

As a Associate on this team, you will be a key member of a small, high performance team, working across two of the largest businesses within Chase - Consumer Bank and Wealth Management. You should be comfortable leading strategic analyses across multiple projects, forming meaningful relationships with internal and external stakeholders, and understanding how to lead through influence across a large, multifaceted organization. You will play a key role in supporting Consumer Bank and Wealth Management's senior executives to evaluate how the financial ecosystem is changing, assess the implications to Chase, and identify external opportunities that will deliver value to our businesses and to Chase's customers. You have outstanding analytical skills, a good eye for attention to detail and regularly produces flawless work, a passion for consumer financial services, and can stay organized across multiple initiatives, and an ability to take initiative with minimal guidance and oversight. 

The Consumer Bank & Wealth Management function in Corporate Development is responsible for strategic partnerships, investments, and acquisitions across Chase's retail deposit and wealth management businesses. The team has three primary functions: 1) identify ways to grow and evolve both businesses through third-party strategies and transactions, 2) lead and execute on all third-party initiatives, including evaluation and negotiation of all transactions, and 3) manage ongoing relationships with existing strategic partners.

Job responsibilities:

Support the evaluation, negotiation, and execution of strategic opportunities for our Consumer Bank and Wealth Management organizations
Collaboratively develop our book of work and pipeline of opportunities with the lines of business, including identifying key elements of the strategy, analysis of the competitive landscape, leading diligence, and making recommendations
Support presentations and proposals to senior executives across the Consumer Bank and Wealth Management
Develop and help deliver specific partner proposals with the lines of business, including overall vision, partnership economics, and product integration
Work with finance, legal and other functional partners to develop business cases, deal constructs and other key terms associated with partnerships
Monitor external environment for important competitive developments and potential partnership opportunities and share perspectives with key line of business partners
Ensure all deals are executed in accordance with firmwide policies, controls and procedures

Required qualifications, capabilities, and skills:

4+ years industry experience, across financial services and/or management consulting; candidate must have at least two years of work experience
BS degree or equivalent experience required
Thrives as an individual contributor in a fast-paced, collaborative, team-oriented, cross functional environment
Outstanding analytical and problem-solving skills
Exceptional oral and written communication skills
Organized, detail-oriented, with strong project management ability 
Able to build relationships inside and outside the company
Intellectual curiosity in fintech industry and ability to learn new subjects quickly
Proficient MS Excel and PowerPoint skills
Prior experience in strategy and/or corporate development at a large institution 
Prior experience in Wealth Management and/or Consumer Banking 

Preferred qualifications, capabilities, and skills:

Prior experience in strategy and/or corporate development at a large institution 
Prior experience in Wealth Management and/or Consumer Banking

Chase is a leading financial services firm, helping nearly half of America's households and small businesses achieve their financial goals through a broad range of financial products. Our mission is to create engaged, lifelong relationships and put our customers at the heart of everything we do. We also help small businesses, nonprofits and cities grow, delivering solutions to solve all their financial needs.

title: L3 - Device Management Specialist
description:
Who We Are

At Kyndryl, we run and reimagine the mission-critical technology systems that drive advantage for the world's leading businesses.  We are at the heart of progress; with proven expertise and a continuous flow of AI-powered insight, enabling smarter decisions, faster innovation, and a lasting competitive edge. For our people-Kyndryls-that means doing purposeful work that powers human progress. Join us and experience a flexible, supportive environment where your well-being is prioritized and your potential can thrive.

The Role

As an L3 Device Management Specialist, you are the Tier‑3 (SME) escalation point for enterprise endpoint management. You ensure reliable, secure and compliant management of Windows, macOS, iOS and Android devices by defining and enforcing standards across enrollment, policies, packaging, patching and compliance. While Workspace ONE tenant administration is part of the role, the primary focus is L3 engineering work: complex troubleshooting, , patch/vulnerability strategy, automation at scale, and delivery governance (rings, pilots, phased rollouts). You lead RCA/Problem activities, secure changes through CAB discipline, and enable L2 through runbooks and coaching.

Who You Are

Key Skills

•  Strong Workspace ONE expertise (policies/profiles, compliance, smart groups, Intelligence, automation)

•

•  Patch/vulnerability management methods (rings, validation, remediation governance)

•  Troubleshooting depth across OSes and UEM components (agent, certificates, policy conflicts)

•  Automation: PowerShell + Bash/Python fundamentals; API usage; Git practices

•  PKI/SCEP fundamentals; Entra ID join and device access principles

•  ITIL v4 (Incident/Problem/Change) and RCA mindset; strong documentation discipline

Nice to have:

Advanced packaging and deployment engineering (Win32/MSIX, macOS pkg, mobile managed apps, scripting)

Languages

•   English: at least B1 level required

•  French or Italian is an advantage

Preferred Certifications

•  Omnissa/VMware Workspace ONE Administrator / Specialist

•  Jamf 200+ / 300+

•  ITIL v4 Foundation

•  Entra ID fundamentals / security baseline exposure

Required Experience

•  3+ years in EUC/UEM/Device Management with Tier‑3 troubleshooting responsibilities

•  Demonstrated experience delivering standards for packaging, patching and compliance at enterprise scale

Being You

The "Kyn" in Kyndryl means kinship, which represents the strong bonds we have with each other, our customers and our communities. We focus on ensuring all Kyndryls feel included and we welcome people of all cultures, backgrounds, and experiences. Even if you don't meet every requirement, we encourage you to apply. We believe in growth, and we're excited to see what you can bring. At Kyndryl, employee feedback has told us that our number one driver of employee engagement is belonging. That sense of belonging - being a valued, respected, trusted member of the team - is fundamental to our culture and fueling great experiences for our customers. This dedication to welcoming everyone into our company means that Kyndryl gives you the ability to thrive and contribute to our culture of empathy and shared success. That's The Kyndryl Way.

What You Can Expect

Your career with us isn't just a job-it's an adventure with purpose.  We offer a dynamic, hybrid-friendly culture that supports your well-being and empowers you to grow. Our Be Well programs are thoughtfully designed to support your financial, mental, physical, and social health-because we know that when you feel your best, you do your best. 

From your very first day, you'll dive into impactful work that powers the systems our customers rely on every day. You won't just contribute-you'll make a difference, tackling meaningful projects that sharpen your skills and fuel your growth.

We're here to champion your journey. With powerful tools to chart your career path, personalized development goals aligned with your ambitions, and continuous feedback to keep you inspired and on track, you'll have everything you need to thrive and evolve. You'll develop in-demand skills to grow your career and achieve your ambitions with access to cutting-edge learning opportunities-from certifications with Microsoft, Google, and Amazon to coaching and hands-on experiences. And through it all, you'll be part of a culture that values empathy, restless learning, and a devotion to shared success. 

We want you to thrive here-and we're committed to helping you do just that. Ready to make an impact? Join us and help shape what's next.

Get Referred! 

If you know someone that works at Kyndryl, when asked 'How Did You Hear About Us' during the application process, select 'Employee Referral' and enter your contact's Kyndryl email address.

title: Asset Management - Fund Controller - Associate
location: Columbus, OH, Jersey City, NJ, New York, NY
description:
Within the Asset Management Client Service division the Product Administration Team and has responsibility for supporting the overall management and oversight of a group of Funds including US Mutual Funds, ETF, and Collective Investment Funds in addition to Canadian products including ETFs. 

Job Summary

As a Asset Management - Fund Controller - Associate you will support the Production Administration leadership team in executing management and oversight responsibilities for the Funds. You will consider the market, regulatory, and business environment that they operate within the space. As a Fund Controller you will participate in and support new fund development and implementation efforts as well as other product related initiatives as they arise. 

Job Responsibilities 

 Execute risk focused oversight model that address all aspects of Fund Operations including: daily/monthly net asset values, distributions, expenses, implementation of accounting policies, issue identification, management and resolution. 
 Evaluate all aspects of proposals (e.g., prospectus language, trading/operational model, distributions, expense structure, etc.) to identify solutions to launch/modify the product.
 Implement the appropriate risk-focused oversight controls. 
 Review and sign off of Funds' financial statements and regulatory filings; coordination of all audit efforts with service providers and external auditors; and, executing disclosure control procedures in support of Audit Committee clearance meetings, principal financial/executive officer certifications, etc. 
 Review and provide input to all Fund-related regulatory filings (e.g., N-1A), participate in efforts to respond to regulatory requests and inquiries related to the Funds. 
 Lead and participate in various Fund related initiatives.
 Develop materials to summarize oversight results to Funds' governing bodies. 
 Develop materials to escalate key issues and status of initiatives.

Required Qualifications, Capabilities, and Skills 

 3+ years' experience in the investment management industry.
 Technical and business knowledge of various Fund structures (e.g., mutual collective investment and ETFs) and activities from an investment, operational, regulatory, accounting and financial reporting perspective.
 Knowledge and experience across various asset classes (e.g., fixed income, alternatives and equities) and complex instrument types (e.g., derivatives and structured products).
 Strong analytical skills with ability to evaluate issues, propose and implement solutions, with consideration for all downstream implications.
 Highly developed interpersonal skills and the ability to work effectively as part of a cross functional team.
 Demonstrated thought leadership and the ability to influence and achieve results. Excellent written, verbal and presentation skills; ability to communicate in a clear and concise manner in any format.
 Proactive attitude, commitment to continuous learning, willing to challenge the status quo to improve processes.
 Flexibility, strong organizational and time management skills.

title: Business Consultant
description:
Job Requisition ID #

26WD99977

Business Consultant - AECO Technical Advisory

Position Overview

Autodesk Consulting is looking for a Business Consultant to join our Northern Europe team. This remote role supports strategic customers across the region.

This is a senior individual contributor role combining business consulting, AECO industry expertise and executive advisory. You'll work with some of Autodesk's largest customers to shape transformation strategies, define target operating models, and develop business cases and roadmaps that deliver measurable business outcomes.

You'll advise senior leaders, structure complex business challenges and lead strategic advisory engagements from discovery through executive decision-making. While you won't configure or implement solutions, you'll understand how Autodesk and complementary technologies fit within customers' broader business and technology ecosystems, partnering with technical specialists to turn strategy into actionable delivery plans.

Main responsibilities

Build trusted relationships with customer executives, business leaders and transformation teams, acting as a strategic advisor throughout the engagement
Understand customer objectives, challenges and operating context to define outcome-driven transformation strategies
Assess operating models, business processes, organizational capabilities, data and digital workflows to identify opportunities for improvement
Define target-state operating models, transformation roadmaps, business cases, success measures and benefits realization plans
Lead executive workshops, facilitate decision-making and align stakeholders across complex organizations
Advise customers on how Autodesk and complementary AECO technologies support business outcomes through effective workflows, data management and interoperability
Identify and prioritize opportunities for data, automation and AI based on business value, organizational readiness, governance and adoption
Partner with Solution Architects, technical consultants and customer-facing teams to shape advisory engagements, validate strategic recommendations and develop credible delivery roadmaps

Minimum Qualifications

Substantial experience in AECO, management consulting or business transformation, with a proven track record of independently leading complex strategy and transformation engagements
Deep expertise in at least one of the following: construction, infrastructure, engineering consultancy, utilities, or a closely related project-based, asset-intensive industry
Strong working knowledge of Autodesk technologies or comparable AECO tool ecosystems, with the ability to discuss capabilities, workflow fit, data, interoperability and business value. Hands-on implementation expertise is not required
Strong understanding of operating models, organizational change, governance, business cases and benefits realization
Practical understanding of data-centric workflows, enterprise systems, automation, responsible AI and technology adoption
Ability to lead through influence across cross-functional and international teams, with excellent communication and executive presentation skills
Fluent English is required. Dutch and other European languages are highly valued
Willingness to travel to customer meetings and Autodesk events across Northern Europe (up to 50%)
Proven experience advising executives, structuring complex problems, facilitating high-stakes workshops and driving decisions

title: Associate, National Provider Contracting
description:
Hi, we're Oscar. We're hiring a Provider Contracting Associate to join our National Contracting team.
 
Oscar is the first health insurance company built around a full stack technology platform and a relentless focus on serving our members. We started Oscar in 2012 to create the kind of health insurance company we would want for ourselves-one that behaves like a doctor in the family.
 
About the role:
 
The Associate, National Contracting manages an assigned portfolio of large national ancillary providers and/or multi-state health systems across the contracting lifecycle-from market assessment and recruitment through negotiation, implementation, performance management, renewal, and escalation. Working with Network leadership and cross-functional partners, this role translates network access and affordability goals into executable contract strategies; uses financial, claims, and provider data to inform negotiations; and maintains durable provider relationships. The Associate helps ensure contracts are operationally sound, compliant, and positioned to deliver high-quality, cost-effective member care across markets.
 
You will report into the Senior Director, Specialty Contracting.
 
Work Location: This is a remote position based in the field, open to candidates who reside: Alabama, Arizona, California, Florida, Illinois, Iowa, Kansas, Michigan, Mississippi, Missouri, Nebraska, New York, North Carolina, Ohio and Texas. Your daily work will involve a blend of work from your home office and frequent local travel for client meetings. Occasional travel may be required for team meetings and company events. #LI-Remote
 
Pay Transparency: Pay Transparency: The base pay for this role in the states of California, Connecticut, New Jersey, New York, and Washington is: $96,876 - $127,149 per year. The base pay for this role in all other locations is: $87,188- $114,434 per year. You are also eligible for employee benefits, participation in Oscar's unlimited vacation program and annual performance bonuses.
 
Responsibilities:
  Support the development and execution of national contracting strategies for large ancillary providers and/or health systems, aligned with network adequacy, access, quality, and cost-management objectives.
 Manage an assigned portfolio across the full contracting lifecycle, including prospecting, evaluation, negotiation, implementation, performance management, renewal, and termination.
 Prepare for and negotiate complex provider agreements, including reimbursement, operational, data-sharing, performance, and compliance terms, within established authority and escalation guidelines.
 Coordinate contract implementation with Legal, Finance, Provider Operations, Claims, Credentialing, Configuration, Compliance, and Market teams to ensure accurate and timely operational readiness.
 Build and maintain productive relationships with provider contracting and operational leaders; lead routine business reviews, resolve escalated issues, and coordinate corrective action plans.
 Analyze claims, utilization, reimbursement, provider roster, market, and competitive data to develop negotiation positions, quantify financial impact, and identify performance improvement opportunities.
 Monitor assigned networks and provider performance for access, adequacy, quality, cost, and contractual compliance; escalate risks and support remediation with Network and Market leadership.
 Maintain accurate contracting pipeline, status, documentation, and provider data; meet defined service-level agreements and performance metrics for outreach, negotiations, and contract completion.
  Compliance with all applicable laws and regulations 
  Other duties as assigned 
  
Requirements:
  3+ years of experience in provider contracting, provider network management, healthcare consulting, healthcare operations, or a related field.
 2+ years of experience supporting provider network strategy and negotiating provider agreements.
 Demonstrated experience managing complex, multi-stakeholder contracting work from analysis and negotiation through implementation and ongoing performance management.
 Experience building effective relationships with provider contracting and operational leaders and communicating recommendations to internal stakeholders.
 1+ years of experience performing financial analysis for healthcare markets, provider contracts, or product lines and translating findings into negotiation or improvement opportunities.
 1+ years of experience working with large data sets, such as claims, utilization, fee schedules, contract inventories, and provider rosters.
  
Bonus points:
  Bachelor's degree in business, healthcare administration, finance, economics, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.
 Experience contracting with national ancillary provider organizations, multi-state provider groups, or large health systems.
 Working knowledge of provider reimbursement methodologies, contract language, claims data, network adequacy, and provider operations.

title: Consultative Offerings - Summer Scholar - Functional & Operations Strategy
location: Atlanta, GA, Austin, TX, Boston, MA, Charlotte, NC, Chicago, IL, Dallas, TX, Denver, CO, Detroit, MI, Houston, TX, Los Angeles, CA, McLean, VA, Minneapolis, MN, New York, NY, Philadelphia, PA, San Francisco, CA, Seattle, WA
description:
Position Summary

Do you want to help executives navigate disruption at a scale and speed they've never faced before? Are you the kind of person who sees a hard problem and leans in instead of looking away? You're exactly who we're looking for.

AI is reshaping industries overnight. Global markets are shifting faster than playbooks can keep up. Entire business models are being rewritten in real time. For the leaders steering through it, this isn't a moment for more of the same...it's a moment that demands fresh thinking, bold moves, and partners who can see around corners. There has never been a more exciting time to be a strategic advisor - join us for this moment!

Is This You?

You're fascinated by the complexity inside organizations: how they're built to perform, how they adapt under pressure, and what it really takes to transform them. You want to master that terrain, and you're ambitious enough to want to be exceptional at it.

You don't need to have it all figured out yet. But you care about creating value for organizations, not just how a plan might read on a page. You're sharp enough to find the signal in messy data. You're genuinely excited about AI, not as a buzzword, but as something you want to learn to use in real, high-stakes situations. And, you want your work to matter starting now, not eventually.

If you want to become the kind of advisor executives trust with their hardest decisions, it starts at Deloitte as a Functional & Operations Strategy Summer Scholar

Recruiting for this role ends on 11/01/2026.  

What You'll Do

Your work will feed the decisions executives can't afford to get wrong.

Here's what that looks like day to day: you'll get a problem that isn't fully defined, and part of your job is figuring out the right question before you can even get to an answer. You'll dig into data, build the analysis, and find the insight that changes how a client sees their situation; you'll be exposed to the latest AI tools and accelerators. You will learn to communicate your recommendation clearly to Executives who've been running companies longer than you've been in the workforce.

The questions you'll wrestle with live at the heart of how organizations function:

How should we modernize our human resources function as AI reshapes what work means, and how do we bring people through that change without losing momentum?
How does the CFO build a finance function that's a true strategic partner, not a reporting machine? What operating model gives a business the agility to execute its strategy at scale?
How do we modernize a supply chain that's one disruption away from breaking?
What does a risk and governance framework look like when it's designed to enable speed, not just prevent failure?
How should a company rethink its physical footprint and infrastructure in a world that keeps shifting underneath it?
How can we configure our Real Estate footprint and workplace to help us achieve our evolving strategic business objectives?
How do we unlock value from core operations to deliver on our company's mission?
How do we move beyond automating old processes to reimagining what's possible with agentic AI?
How can leaders build a customer experience that is seamless across every channel? What combination of customer strategy, data, technology, and operating model turns moments of interaction into lasting relationships?
How does an organization become truly customer-centric - not just in its marketing, but across sales, service, product, and operations? What capabilities and ways of working make customer obsession scalable?

These are the questions our clients bring to us because they trust that no one is more equipped to answer them.

The work spans the full arc of strategic advising: diagnosing where a business function stands, charting where it needs to go, and designing the transformation required to get there. You'll be expected to think, not just execute, and to bring a perspective into every conversation.

 Our CrowdStrike Data Science Machine Learning Operations and Response Team is looking for a Threat Analyst who is both customer- and team-focused.  Perform tasks to enable better-management of false positive detections
 Analyze binary files to determine their legitimacy
 Review current product detections to ensure they are performing to the company standard

 Knowledge of programming and scripting languages, in particular Python

 Ability to demonstrate practical knowledge of research/collection skills and analytical methods

 Ability to break down complex problems into workable components
 Proven experience utilizing AI technologies to enhance decision-making, streamline workflows and processes, improve efficiency and drive business outcomes.

description:
Position Summary

Do you want to help executives navigate disruption at a scale and speed they've never faced before? Are you the kind of person who sees a hard problem and leans in instead of looking away? You're exactly who we're looking for.

AI is reshaping industries overnight. Global markets are shifting faster than playbooks can keep up. Entire business models are being rewritten in real time. For the leaders steering through it, this isn't a moment for more of the same...it's a moment that demands fresh thinking, bold moves, and partners who can see around corners. There has never been a more exciting time to be a strategic advisor - join us for this moment!

Is This You?

You're fascinated by the complexity inside organizations: how they're built to perform, how they adapt under pressure, and what it really takes to transform them. You want to master that terrain, and you're ambitious enough to want to be exceptional at it.

You don't need to have it all figured out yet. But you care about creating value for organizations, not just how a plan might read on a page. You're sharp enough to find the signal in messy data. You're genuinely excited about AI, not as a buzzword, but as something you want to learn to use in real, high-stakes situations. And, you want your work to matter starting now, not eventually.

Recruiting for this role ends on 11/01/2026.

How do we modernize a supply chain that's one disruption away from breaking?
